Olga — thanks for flagging. Quick notes from legal triage: 
1) "Written consent" is high risk for us operationally; it could create blockers for autoscaling/ops. We should propose a middle ground: notification + 10 business day objection period for material changes, with an express carve-out for infra-level / cloud provider substitutions.
2) Evidence package: propose we offer our standard bundle (SOC2 Type II + subprocessors matrix + on-demand attestation). If they insist on per-subprocessor SAQs, we can offer to reference the attestation process instead of producing every SAQ preemptively.
3) For EU analytics vendors: if processing occurs in EU and the customer requires EU residency, we can accept contractual commitments but may need to coordinate with infra to pin regions or use dedicated capacity.

Action items: Olga to propose the compromise language to EdgeFlow; Laura to prep the SOC2/attestation bundle and a short note on residency options.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Olga,

Thanks for the quick triage. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The written consent ask is primarily a procurement control for certain regulated customers; it doesn't block infra-level substitutions but does require explicit sign-off for adding a new analytics subprocessor in the initial 12 months after contract execution.
- For evidence, SOC2 + subprocessors matrix is fine, but their procurement team has historically requested per-subprocessor questionnaires for any vendor that touches PII.

We understand your staffing/ops concerns and are open to the 10-business-day objection window you proposed. Would Redwood accept: "Supplier will notify Customer of intent to add a subprocessor and allow Customer up to 10 business days to object; if not objected to in writing, consent is deemed granted" plus an infra carve-out?

We can also add a clause that requires EdgeFlow to provide reasonable evidence upon request for any newly added subprocessor (e.g., SOC/ISO certs or completed SAQs).

If you can send redline language, we'll circulate internally and aim to respond within 3 business days.

Thanks — Laura here from Solutions/Privacy ops. We're OK with the proposed 10 business day objection window with the infra carve-out. Draft redline below (insert into §4.2):

"Supplier shall notify Customer at least ten (10) business days prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will process Customer Personal Data. Customer shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of such notification to object in writing on reasonable grounds relating to data protection. If Customer does not object within such period, Customer's consent shall be deemed granted. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Supplier may engage replacements or alternative infrastructure-level subprocessors (including cloud provider swaps) without such advance notification where Supplier reasonably determines the change is required for operational continuity; Supplier will notify Customer of such infrastructure-level changes as soon as reasonably practicable."

Additionally, we'll provide our SOC2 package + subprocessors matrix via the Drive link and will accept providing per-subprocessor questionnaires upon receipt of a legitimate written request from Procurement.

If EdgeFlow sign off on language, Laura will circulate a clean MSA excerpt and Olivia (Ops) will trigger the evidence bundle.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
